run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-259 had issues on November 21, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: Only Grafana Loki was reachable in this Run; Prometheus, Jaeger and the Kubernetes API all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every query attempted, so pod status, restarts, ConfigMaps, traces and error-rate series could not be checked. What Loki shows for namespace app-259: the single observed pod payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 (job=payment-api, service=payment-api) logged only two message types in the 24h authorized window — 24 'Payment processed successfully' lines and 8 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' error lines. The pool-exhausted errors are confined to 2026-11-21 13:46–14:44 UTC, with wait_time_ms between 1227 and 4840 and queue_length between 5 and 15; before 13:46 and after 14:44 the sampled lines are successes only. Successful payments were also logged at 13:42, 13:59 and 14:49, i.e. the pod kept serving while a share of requests failed to get a database connection. The deep cause of the pool exhaustion (the database itself, a pool-size/concurrency configuration, or a burst of traffic) is unknown because the dependency's own signals were unreachable and no Kubernetes object could be read; no root-cause object can be named.

claims.text: The only log stream returned for namespace app-259 in the authorized window is job=payment-api / service=payment-api, pod_name=payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12; it produced 32 log lines in total across the 24h window (2026-11-21T10:02:59Z–2026-11-22T10:02:59Z).

Exactly two distinct log messages exist for that pod in the whole window: 'Payment processed successfully' (24 lines) and 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' (8 lines at level ERROR).

All eight 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' ERROR lines of pod payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 fall between 2026-11-21T13:46:00Z and 2026-11-21T14:44:00Z: at 13:46 (wait_time_ms 1227, queue_length 10), 13:54 (2104, 11), 14:03 (1495, 8), 14:15 (2965, 9), 14:19 (4005, 10), 14:21 (4840, 8), 14:31 (2358, 15) and 14:44 (3836, 5).

The 10-minute count of ERROR lines for the pod is zero in every bucket before the bucket ending 2026-11-21T13:47:40Z, becomes non-zero from that bucket onward through the bucket ending 2026-11-21T14:50:33Z (values 1,1,1,1,1,1,3,2,1,1,1,1), and afterwards only the INFO series continues.

Before the error burst, from 2026-11-21T10:02:59Z to 13:00:00Z, the pod's sampled logs contain only INFO 'Payment processed successfully' lines (11:19, 11:40, 11:44, 12:57) and no ERROR line was returned.

Successful payments were logged inside and immediately after the error window — 13:42 (PAY-5032), 13:59 (PAY-1800), 14:49 (PAY-8206) and 15:27 (PAY-4120) — so the pod continued to process some payments rather than failing completely.

A line-filter over the pod's logs for 'pool|connection|timeout|config|restart|start|shutdown|database' in 13:30–15:00 returned only the eight pool-exhausted ERROR lines, i.e. no restart, startup, shutdown or pool-configuration log line was returned for that interval.

Against a total-outage reading: the same pod logged completed payments at 13:42 and 13:59 during the failure window and at 14:49 and 15:27 after it, and no ERROR line was returned after 14:44 through the end of the authorized window, so the observed condition is intermittent connection-acquisition failure, not a pod-wide stop.

The failures originated inside payment-api's own database connection pool: requests waited 1.2–4.8 s and queued 5–15 deep before giving up, which points to connections being held or the pool being sized below the concurrent demand. The identity of the database and whether it was slow, saturated or refusing connections is unknown, because no metric, trace or cluster object for a database dependency could be read.

A pod restart or rollout at ~13:45 as the trigger is not supported by the log evidence: the pod name is unchanged across the whole window, all lines carry the same pod_name payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12, and a filter for restart/start/shutdown lines returned nothing. Pod status, restart counts and ReplicaSet history could not be read (Kubernetes API unavailable), so this is not excluded, only unsupported.

Read the payment-api Deployment/Pod in app-259 (status, containerStatuses lastState/restartCount, events) and its ConfigMap/env for connection-pool settings, then compare with the database dependency's own saturation metrics and the payment spans covering 13:45–14:45 — none of which were observable in this Run.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable (get_metric_names, get_label_values, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query, list_prometheus_rules, get_prometheus_target all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no error-rate, latency, pool-size or saturation series and no alert state existed for this investigation; ERROR metrics are unknown, not zero.
Jaeger was unreachable (traces_list_services and traces_search returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no span-level attribution of the failing payment operation or of its database call is available.

The Kubernetes API was unreachable (kubernetes_jq_query and kubernetes_tabular_query returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for pods and events), so pod phase, readiness, restart counts, last termination reason, ReplicaSet/Deployment ownership, events, ConfigMaps, Services, endpoints, networkpolicies and resourcequotas were not checked.

The identity and health of the database dependency behind 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' is unknown; the log message names no host, pool size or upstream service, and no dependency-level telemetry was reachable.

No baseline before 2026-11-21T10:02:59Z exists in the authorized window, so whether 8 pool-exhausted errors are above this pod's normal rate cannot be established; the log stream is also sparse (32 sampled lines in 24h), so error and success counts are lower bounds on actual occurrences.
Change history is not integrated, so whether a configuration or deployment change preceded 13:46 could not be examined.
next_steps: Fetch pod/Deployment state and events for payment-api in app-259 (restartCount, lastState, Unhealthy/BackOff events) once the Kubernetes API is reachable.
Inspect payment-api environment/ConfigMap for connection-pool settings (max pool size, acquisition timeout, max lifetime) and compare them with observed wait_time_ms 1227–4840 and queue_length 5–15.

Check the database dependency's own CPU, connection-count and latency metrics, and payment/database spans for 2026-11-21T13:40–14:50Z, to decide whether the pool was undersized or the database was slow.
Confirm whether callers of payment-api (e.g. checkout/frontend) saw failed payment operations in 13:45–14:45 before attributing customer impact.
